Verdict: approve.

Approve: nuclear enlargement is large and consistent across 0.1-3 μM (nuc_area z≈20-27, integrated DNA up) while tubulin remains near baseline until ≥3-10 μM, supporting a potent primary nuclear MoA over Microtubule stabilizers. In the mid-dose atlas, the three highest-similarity neighbours are DNA damage (0.93-0.97) from multiple references, versus lower-similarity DNA replication neighbours dominated by one reference series (≈0.87), so 0.65 vs 0.20 is reasonably calibrated. ## Unblinding

Compound: **mitomycin C** (PubChem CID [5746](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5746))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **DNA damage**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA damage**.

## Reflection

The call was correct because I prioritized the reproducible mid-dose nuclear phenotype over the dramatic high-dose cytoskeletal phenotype. Wells at 0.1, 0.3, 1 and 3 uM all showed nuc_area z +20.5 to +26.7 with 399-637 cells and increased integrated DNA, while tubulin remained near baseline until 3-10 uM; the mid-dose atlas comparison giving DNA damage 5/10 with top neighbours 0.93-0.97 then outranked DNA replication neighbours at ~0.87, consistent with mitomycin C crosslink damage reported in PMID 41199376 and PMID 17512921.

I was misled by the high-dose acquisitions: well w_b962c28c9c at 10 uM with only 155 cells showed tub_glcm_contrast z +25.1, replicated in w_c1033d961b with act_std z +39.1, plus atlas e9 with Microtubule stabilizers 8/10 and microscopist e6 suggesting stabilizers. The e7 Aurora suggestion at mid-dose and the flat nuc_area dose-response rho -0.20 p=0.8 also looked like weak dose-dependence until I recognized it as early saturation from 0.1 uM onward, while tub_glcm_contrast rho +1.00 and cell_count rho -1.00 marked late toxicity.

The key acquisition choices were acquiring the 0.1 uM onset well e14 and the 10 uM replicate e15, which proved the nuclear effect was potent and reproducible and the bundling was confined to severely depleted wells. Residual uncertainty between DNA damage 0.65 and DNA replication 0.20 was appropriate given shared fork-arrest biology noted in PMID 23319047, and was resolved by weighting multi-reference high-similarity damage neighbours over single-series replication neighbours.

What was right:
- Prioritized potent reproducible nuclear enlargement (nuc_area z +20.5 to +26.7, nuc_major_axis z +10.9 to +15.4, nuc_dna_integrated z +14.0) across 0.1-3 uM in 4 wells with 399-637 cells as primary MoA
- Used mid-dose atlas e8 DNA damage 5/10 with top similarities 0.93-0.97 to outrank DNA replication neighbours and correctly down-weight high-dose atlas e9 stabilizers 8/10 as late effect
- Treated high-dose tubulin/actin texture (tub_glcm_contrast z +25.1, act_std z +39.1) with marked cell loss to 155-160 cells and cell_count rho -1.00 as secondary toxicity since tubulin was intact at nuclear-effective doses

What was wrong or missed:
- High-dose bundling plus e6 Microtubule stabilizers visual call transiently favored stabilizer hypothesis despite intact mid-dose tubulin
- Mid-dose visual e7 suggesting Aurora kinase inhibitors and flat nuc_area dose-response rho -0.20 p=0.8 could have been misread as lack of dose-dependence rather than saturation from 0.1 uM
- Did not mechanistically separate DNA damage from DNA replication beyond atlas similarity levels, leaving 0.65 vs 0.20 calibration dependent on review

Proposed next experiment: Stain for gamma-H2AX/53BP1 foci with DNA-content flow cytometry for G2 arrest across 0.03-3 uM mitomycin C, plus washout to test persistence of crosslink-induced arrest versus the transient high-dose cytoskeletal toxicity at 10 uM.

- PMID [23319047](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23319047/): Lamin A/C depletion enhances DNA damage-induced stalled replication fork arrest. *Mol Cell Biol* (2013) — DNA damage-induced stalled replication fork arrest explains the phenotypic overlap between DNA damage and DNA replication atlas classes.
